purpose: Founder Observation Quality + cross-market source/relevance benchmark. Synthetic hypotheses are test inputs only and have zero market-truth authority.

execution_policy.holdout_rule: Do not use HOLDOUT cases to tune relevance/routing before the first holdout run.
notes: GOLDEN cases have manual relevance expectations.
TOURNAMENT_MAIN cases come from prior AI opportunity tournaments and remain synthetic/unvalidated.
HOLDOUT exists to detect overfitting after quality repair.

records.title: AI coding agents finish work but founders cannot efficiently verify whether the work is actually correct and complete
records.description: Founders using Claude Code, Codex or similar coding agents need to verify requirements, tests, correctness and actual completion without manually reviewing everything.

annotation.exact_relevance: Completion verification, requirement adherence, tests/acceptance evidence, human review burden, claimed completion vs actual result.
annotation.adjacent_not_exact: General AI coding complaints, agent orchestration, productivity, coding experience.
known_negative_examples: AI coding made me faster, but I can't code to music anymore
Spit Notes – lyrics and voice memos
annotation.known_positive_example: AI cannot always be trusted to understand changed functionality or requirements, so human review remains useful or essential.

records.title: Compressed-Air Leak Detection / Recovery
records.description: SME factories with pneumatic equipment may waste electricity through compressed-air leaks; the customer buys identification of where money is leaking and what to fix.

annotation.stress_question: Is this a recurring market pain or merely a one-off on-site service?

records.title: PCBA First-Article Inspection Acceleration
records.description: EMS/PCBA QA teams may face first-article inspection bottlenecks after SMT line changes; the hypothesis is that faster BOM/placement/visual verification can reduce release delay.

annotation.stress_question: Do existing AOI/SPI/FAI systems already solve the economically important gap?

records.title: Machine Downtime Log Intelligence
records.description: Production managers may have machine fault and downtime logs but still struggle to identify which recurring causes produce the largest real output loss.

annotation.stress_question: Does the analysis reveal new actionable learning or merely restate what operators already know?

records.title: Scrap / Byproduct Competitive Bidding
records.description: Factories that repeatedly sell metal scrap or production byproducts may accept fixed recycler pricing; competitive bids could expose price uplift and create a recurring transaction network.

annotation.stress_question: Are price spreads meaningful after logistics, relationships and settlement terms?

records.title: Raw-Material Group Purchasing
records.description: Small manufacturers with insufficient individual order volume may combine recurring purchases to reach supplier bulk-price tiers.

annotation.stress_question: Do timing, specifications, delivery, credit and MOQ coordination destroy the economics?

records.title: Solar Warranty Recovery / Inspection Targeting
records.description: Solar asset owners may need to identify financially meaningful underperformance before warranty or defect-liability deadlines and target physical inspection where evidence is most valuable.

annotation.stress_question: What evidence do OEMs actually accept, and how much value can software add before physical testing is required?

records.title: Construction Claim / Change-Order Evidence
records.description: Contractors may struggle to prove extra work, timing, instructions and approvals in change-order disputes, delaying or reducing payment.

annotation.stress_question: Does better evidence materially change claim approval and payment outcomes?

records.title: Industrial Tariff / Contract-Capacity Correction
records.description: SME factories may incur avoidable electricity cost from contract-capacity choices, tariff structure, peak demand or power-factor issues.
